page.title: Bigger Ways To Help
page.description: Volunteering, effective giving, kindred sites and newsletters worth your time — the places I'd point a friend to.
intro: Casually generous is meant to sit alongside the big stuff, not replace it. Regular volunteering and well-chosen giving can do things a free afternoon can't — and if something on this site sparks that, brilliant.
These are the places I'd point a friend to. Nobody's paying to be here, and I've kept each list short on purpose.

sections.title: Sites Like This One
sections.intro: Other people working on the same idea — making everyday kindness easier to start.

items.name: Doing Good Together
items.blurb: Kindness and volunteering ideas built for families, with lots for doing good alongside kids. US-based, but most ideas travel well.

items.name: DoSomething
items.blurb: Campaigns and practical actions for young people who want to change something in their community. Mostly US, aimed at 13–25s.

sections.title: Volunteering
sections.intro: When you're ready to give regular time, these make it much easier to find something that fits.

items.name: Do-it
items.blurb: The UK's big volunteering database. Put in your postcode and browse what local groups and charities actually need.

items.name: Reach Volunteering
items.blurb: Skills-based volunteering for UK charities — handy if you'd rather offer what you do at work than a Saturday morning.
items._note: Not re-verified this round — check site is live before shipping.

items.name: Idealist
items.blurb: Volunteer roles, internships and jobs at social-impact organisations, mostly US-based. Now also home to what was VolunteerMatch.

sections.title: Giving Well
sections.intro: I don't pick charities myself. These independent evaluators do the hard research on where money goes furthest.

items.name: GiveWell
items.blurb: Deep, public research into global health and poverty charities, with clear explanations of why each one makes the cut.
items._note: Well-established; quick live check before shipping.

items.name: Giving Green
items.blurb: Evidence-based recommendations for climate giving, and more recently biodiversity too. Updated every year.

items.name: Giving What We Can
items.blurb: A friendly starting point for giving more thoughtfully, pulling together recommendations from several evaluators in one place.
items._note: Well-established; quick live check before shipping.

items.name: The Life You Can Save
items.blurb: A short, approachable list of vetted charities working on extreme poverty, plus a free book on why it matters.
items._note: Well-established; quick live check before shipping.

sections.title: Newsletters Worth Reading
sections.intro: A few inboxes that leave me a bit more hopeful (and a bit more curious) than before I opened them.

items.name: Reasons to be Cheerful
items.blurb: Weekly solutions journalism about problems people are actually solving. Their monthly Spark email focuses on how to get involved.

items.name: Dense Discovery
items.blurb: A beautifully put-together weekly on design, tech, sustainability and living more considerately. Human-curated every issue.

items.name: Recomendo
items.blurb: Six tiny recommendations every Sunday morning. Not about generosity, but generous in spirit, and the most reliably good email I get.
items._note: Newsletter confirmed active (Kevin Kelly, weekly). URL NOT confirmed — find the current signup link before shipping.

items.name: Positive News
items.blurb: UK-based constructive journalism about what's going right, from climate to community. A good antidote to doomscrolling.

items.name: Good News Network
items.blurb: A long-running daily dose of good news from around the world. Light, quick and reliably uplifting.
items._note: Not re-verified this round. Lighter in tone than the others — keep only if you genuinely read it.
